subject: storytime
title: The Bremen Town Musicians
about: The Brothers Grimm's tale of a donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster who are all too old to be wanted, so they set off together to be musicians in the town of Bremen. First graders love the growing chorus of hee-haw, woof, meow and cock-a-doodle-doo, the animal pile-up at the window and the robbers who run from a noise, and the ending says plainly that friends who work together are never too old to help. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Say the four animal sounds together, louder each time, then ask why the robbers ran away.

book.author: the Brothers Grimm (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Four old friends, one big noise, and a snug new home.

passage.text:
Once there was an old donkey.
He was too old to carry sacks.
"No one needs me now," he said sadly.
"I will go to Bremen and be a musician."
Soon he met an old dog.
"I am too old to hunt," said the dog.
"Come with me!" said the donkey.
"We will be musicians in Bremen!"
Hee-haw! Woof!
***
Next they met an old cat.
"I am too old to catch mice," said the cat.
"Come with us!" said the donkey.
"We will be musicians in Bremen!"
Then they met an old rooster.
"No one wants me on the farm," said the rooster.
"Come with us!" said the cat.
"We will be musicians in Bremen!"
Hee-haw! Woof! Meow! Cock-a-doodle-doo!
***
Night came.
The four friends were tired and hungry.
Then they saw a light in the woods.
It was a little cottage.
They peeked in the window.
Three robbers sat at a big table.
They had bread and cheese and cake!
"I have a plan," said the donkey.
"Let's make some music."
***
The dog got on the donkey's back.
The cat got on the dog's back.
The rooster got on top of the cat.
Then they all sang at once.
Hee-haw! Woof! Meow! Cock-a-doodle-doo!
What a terrible noise!
The robbers jumped up.
"What is that?" they yelled.
They ran far, far away.
They never came back.
***
The four friends went inside.
They ate the bread and cheese and cake.
The cat slept by the warm fire.
The rooster slept up on a beam.
They never did get to Bremen.
But they did not mind.
They stayed in the snug cottage.
Friends who work together are never too old to help.

cards.q: What was the donkey too old to do?
cards.note: An old donkey cannot carry heavy sacks any more, so he sets off to make music instead.

cards.q: Where did the four friends want to go?
cards.note: Bremen is a town; the four friends head there to sing for their supper, though they never arrive.

cards.q: Who stood at the very top?
cards.note: Donkey, then dog, then cat, then rooster: the smallest climbs on top.

cards.q: What did the robbers do when they heard the noise?
cards.note: They never found out that the terrible noise was four old animals saying hello.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Too old to carry sacks, the donkey leaves home to be a musician; everything else follows.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: They never reached Bremen and did not mind: they had a snug cottage and each other.

cards.q: How did the donkey feel at the start?
cards.note: Nobody needed him any more; ask what cheered him up again.
Alone, each friend was too old to be wanted; together they won a warm home.

cards.q: In the story, what is a 'musician'?
cards.note: A musician makes music by singing or playing; the friends plan to sing for their supper.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
